topSignals.title: Bloom Energy + MiTAC Fremont: SOFC-islanded microgrid at AI server manufacturing campus (August 6, first appearance)
topSignals.text: — Bloom Energy announced an expanded partnership with MiTAC Computing Technology Corp. on August 6, adding an islanded fuel cell microgrid at MiTAC's AI server manufacturing campus in Fremont, California. The deployment adds to an existing Bloom system at MiTAC's San Jose facility, increasing total contracted on-site capacity across both California sites. Bloom now serves nearly two dozen AI infrastructure customers with approximately 250 MW of contracted capacity — up from essentially zero two years ago. Evercore ISI reiterated an Outperform rating and $350 price target following the announcement, with analyst Nicholas Amicucci noting "AI reach is deeper than investors thought." Bloom Energy PR | Evercore/TipRanks | Benzinga

topSignals.title: FERC RM26-4: CAISO fast-tracks November compliance filing; ISO-NE tables "Bring Your Own Generation" requirement — 8 days to August 17 hard deadline
topSignals.text: — New details have emerged on how CAISO and ISO-NE are responding to FERC's June 18 show cause orders (the two operators whose treatment was unclear after PJM, MISO, NYISO, and SPP received direct "revise tariff" orders on August 8). CAISO is fast-tracking a stakeholder compliance process aimed at a November filing (consistent with an abeyance grant). ISO-NE has proposed a "Bring Your Own Generation" (BYOG) requirement for large loads: new data center and industrial customers seeking interconnection would be required to demonstrate access to on-site generation as a condition of interconnection approval. If adopted, BYOG would structurally mandate on-site firm power for all new large loads in ISO-NE territory — making SOFC systems a regulatory necessity, not merely an economic choice. August 17 tariff-reform deadline remains 8 days out. Akin — FERC Launches ISO-NE Section 206 | Akin — FERC Launches CAISO Section 206 | Climate Solutions Law — RTO/ISO Preview

topSignals.title: Rystad Energy: fuel cell market to reach $30B by 2030, SOFC system costs to fall 20-25% — first appearance
topSignals.text: — Published in late June 2026, Rystad Energy's definitive market sizing of the data center fuel cell opportunity has not previously appeared in this digest. Key figures: global fuel cell market revenues surge from ~$2.8B in 2025 to ~$30B by 2030 (10x increase), driven almost entirely by AI data centers. Cumulative DC fuel cell demand 2026-2030: 10.4 GW. Roughly 40% of projected 2030 US data center capacity modeled as pursuing on-site generation. SOFC system costs expected to fall 20-25% by 2030 as manufacturing scales. Scandium supply chain bottleneck (Bloom's primary rare earth dependency) is identified as the key risk to the base case. Manufacturing output on track for 4 GW/yr capacity by 2030 vs. 1.8 GW/yr today. LCOE flag. Rystad Energy | OilPrice | Gasworld

items.text: Elcogen (priority): Quiet day August 9. Status unchanged: E3000 G2 — >75% FC electrical efficiency (stack-level LHV), 90% total with heat recovery, 23,000 rapid current cycles in SOEC mode with performance improvement, zero thermal-cycling degradation (EFCF 2026 / ResearchGate paper). ELCO I Tallinn factory (360 MW/yr) in volume production and delivering G2 stacks. €140M total funding secured. Next watch: full peer-reviewed EFCF paper and system-level efficiency confirmation at ELCO I production scale. Elcogen

Topsoe (priority): Quiet day August 9. Status unchanged: Herning SOEC factory (500 MW/yr) hibernated pending commercial-scale H2 demand recovery; CEO Elena Scaltritti (since June 1, 2026); FY2026 guidance DKK 7,600-8,400M revenue, EBIT margin 4-9%. SOFC/data-center pathway deferred to 2029+. Topsoe.com
Other players: Quiet day. No new announcements from Bloom (technology), Ceres Power (stack), SolydEra, FuelCell Energy (stack-level), Mitsubishi Power, Kyocera, or Aisin.

Bloom Energy + MiTAC Fremont islanded microgrid (August 6, first appearance): See Top Signal #1. Key detail: Fremont campus is an AI server manufacturing facility — not a data center in the traditional sense. This marks the first confirmed SOFC deployment at an AI hardware manufacturer's campus (vs. hyperscaler or colocation DC), broadening the addressable market definition. Total Bloom AI customer count: ~24 customers, ~250 MW. Customer list beyond the previously named (Oracle, Nebius, Brookfield, AEP, Equinix) confirmed to be wider than the market estimated. Bloom Energy PR

Oracle Project Jupiter (2.45 GW, New Mexico): No new update on the dismiss motion. The hearing officer ordered developers (Yucca Growth Infrastructure) to respond to the New Energy Economy dismiss motion by last Tuesday — watch NMED docket for the ruling. The September 14 public hearing date remains threatened if the dismiss motion is granted. Developer attorneys cited $325M/month carrying costs as the basis for the original September rescheduling request; a dismiss ruling would halt proceedings entirely pending fuel supply solution. No new filings identified for August 9. ABQ Journal | NMELC

Active pipeline carry-forward: Crusoe/Cheyenne (900 MW Phase 1 Bloom SOFCs, first data halls H2 2026), FCEL/Fit Energy (380 MW total, 30 MW initial delivery H2 2026), Equinix >100 MW (19+ DCs), Bloom/Brookfield $25B framework, Nebius 328 MW EaaS, Delta Electronics Q4 2026 production ramp (Ceres Endura).

FERC RM26-4 — August 17 deadline in 8 days; CAISO and ISO-NE positions clarified: See Top Signal #2. CAISO: fast-tracking a November compliance filing (abeyance likely granted for 90 days, putting the deadline to November 16). ISO-NE: proposing a "Bring Your Own Generation" requirement for large loads — a structural rule change that would make on-site firm power mandatory for new hyperscale data center interconnection in New England. Direct "revise tariff" orders already issued to PJM, MISO, NYISO, and SPP (August 8). The picture after August 17: four operators filing tariff revisions (activating the $5-20/MWh avoided-T-cost benefit), CAISO targeting November, ISO-NE potentially adopting BYOG with a separate November-range filing. Climate Solutions Law | Akin/Lexology CAISO | FERC RM26-4 docket

Background unchanged: NY data center moratorium (50 MW+, EO 62, islanded exemption active); Germany EnEfG PUE ≤1.2 / ERF ≥10% / 15% waste heat reuse from July 2026; EU CADA energy efficiency rating scheme delayed; ITC 48E 30% credit active for all fuel cell feedstocks; ERCOT Batch Zero self-supply pathway active.

ISO-NE "Bring Your Own Generation" proposal: If adopted, BYOG creates a regulatory obligation for on-site firm power at any large load seeking ISO-NE interconnection — effectively eliminating the choice between SOFC and grid connection for large data centers in New England (Maine, New Hampshire, Vermont, Massachusetts, Connecticut, Rhode Island). The only commercially available, rapidly deployable, 24/7 firm on-site generation technology at the required scale is SOFC. The proposal is not yet final; watch for FERC's response to ISO-NE's August 17 filing.

Background unchanged from August 8: Blue Energy/GE Vernova/Crusoe gas-to-nuclear 2.5 GW (Phase 1 gas 2030, BWRX-300 2032); Holtec/Entergy/Hyundai E&C dual SMR-300 MOA Gulf South (2033+); Microsoft TMI Unit 1 restart (835 MW, first electrons 2027 — grid restart, not new build); Meta/Oklo 1.2 GW Pike County OH (2030+); Microsoft Project Kilby 2.67 GW CCGT Texas (first power 2028); TVA/Kairos Power/Google 50 MW PPA (Hermes 2 FHR, 2030 first power). SOFC 90-day deployment advantage unchallenged through 2029.

Bloom Energy (BE): Evercore ISI reiterates Outperform $350 on expanded MiTAC partnership (August 6 announcement). "AI reach is deeper than investors thought." Q3 FY2026 earnings (October) is next catalyst. Analyst range: B. Riley Buy $32 | Jefferies Buy $24 | UBS Neutral $22. CNBC FCEL

Ceres Power (LON: CWR): Goldman Sachs August Conviction Buy (168% upside) unchanged. Delta Electronics Q4 2026 production ramp (Ceres Endura 10.8 kW stack) is the next execution catalyst before H1 2026 results (September). Stock down ~15% in August to date on broader AI spending sentiment. TheStreet/Goldman
Market sizing (Rystad): Fuel cell market $2.8B (2025) → $30B (2030); 10.4 GW cumulative DC demand; manufacturing capacity to 4 GW/yr by 2030. See Top Signal #3.

"Comprehensive review of current trends and future directions of metal-supported solid oxide fuel cell: From materials to applications" (International Journal of Minerals, Metallurgy and Materials, Springer, 2026, DOI: 10.1007/s12613-026-3402-0) — Comprehensive review of MS-SOFCs (metal-supported SOFCs) covering thin electrolytes, mixed ionic-electronic conductors, chromium poisoning mitigation, and advanced manufacturing techniques. Key advantage of MS-SOFC architecture vs. conventional ceramic: rapid thermal cycling, enhanced mechanical stability under prolonged operation, lower manufacturing cost, and high electrochemical performance under conditions relevant to dynamic data center load-following. Not system-level TEA, but materials roadmap relevant for estimating the stack cost trajectory toward the $1,000/kW target. Springer IJMMM
Quiet day otherwise for new IP/patent filings.

lcoe.text: Rystad SOFC system cost reduction (new): 20-25% by 2030. From current base-case $5,800-6,500/kW, Rystad's trajectory projects $4,350-5,200/kW by 2030 at current manufacturing scale-up pace. Add as a "2030 cost curve" sensitivity alongside the base-case and optimistic scenarios. At $4,500/kW and 30% ITC 48E credit: effective net capex $3,150/kW — approaching competitiveness with new CCGT capex ($2,000-2,200/kW) without the grid interconnection premium. Rystad Energy

ISO-NE BYOG regulatory scenario: If adopted, on-site generation is no longer optional for new large-load interconnection in New England. Model as a "BYOG-mandated" scenario in which SOFC LCOE is compared against grid cost + BYOG penalty (effectively: SOFC competes against nothing, as it IS the compliance solution). Add as an upper-bound demand scenario for ISO-NE region market sizing.

Bloom + MiTAC Fremont: AI manufacturing as new SOFC market segment. First confirmed SOFC deployment at an AI server manufacturing facility (not a DC or hyperscaler). Suggests addressable market for SOFC extends to the full AI infrastructure supply chain — manufacturing campuses, assembly facilities, HPC cooling infrastructure — not just DC campuses. No direct LCOE impact, but relevant for market sizing upstream of data center deployments.
